what_it_does: Designing analog circuits (circuits that work with continuously varying voltages, like amplifiers) requires running SPICE simulations — detailed physics-based calculations that are notoriously slow and expensive, sometimes taking hours for a single design. Neural surrogate models (machine learning models trained to mimic the simulator) can predict circuit behavior much faster, but most are tied to a specific chip manufacturing process or require large amounts of training data. INSIGHT reframes analog performance prediction as a language-model-style task: it encodes a circuit's structure and parameters as a sequence and uses a transformer (the same class of model behind modern AI chatbots) to predict performance metrics one by one in order, each prediction informed by the previous ones. To adapt the model to a new chip manufacturing process without retraining from scratch, it uses LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation — a technique that adjusts only a small fraction of the model's parameters, keeping most of them frozen), which cuts required training data by 60% and reduces memory use and training time by roughly 42% and 25% respectively.
